checkpoints.description: [1/6] Build Cairn: an agent-first language with its own x86-64 backend that emits Windows PE executables directly, no C toolchain

impact_assessment.why: The user wants a new language whose internals are easy for AI agents to learn, with machine-level speed and its own compiler rather than a C backend.
impact_assessment.benefits: One numeric type and one obvious syntax remove ambiguity for agents; direct machine-code emission gives zero-cost semantics, no libc, no external toolchain, and deterministic binaries
impact_assessment.risks: contract: language surface and CLI are new, so they must be frozen in an ADR; dependency: Python 3.10+ bootstrap only, stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: builds are written atomically and are byte-reproducible
impact_assessment.mitigation: Freeze v0.1 in ADR-001, keep the backend behind a documented instruction set subset, cover every stage with failing-first unit tests plus end-to-end runs of the produced .exe, and run every project gate

checkpoints.description: [2/6-5/6] Implemented the compiler: lexer, parser, sema with slots, x86-64 emitter, print and divide-by-zero helpers as machine code, PE32+ writer with imports and fixups, atomic build pipeline and CLI

handoff.state: all modules under cairn/, 4 examples, 65 tests
handoff.evidence: examples/fib.crn prints 55 and 5050 from a 2048-byte exe

checkpoints.description: [6/6] Verified: 65 tests pass in 0.3s, 4/4 gates pass (test, hygiene, guidelines, secrets), builds are byte-reproducible, end-to-end executables run and match expected output; checklists: passed

handoff.state: v0.1 surface frozen in ADR-001, backend in ADR-002, diagnostics in ADR-003, performance claim in ADR-004
handoff.open: no optimiser and no aggregate types, both recorded as non-goals

checkpoints.description: [1/6] Add an optimiser pass, a register fast path in codegen, and a reproducible benchmark harness with an optional C baseline

impact_assessment.why: Cairn 0.1 proves the pipeline but has no optimiser and no repeatable way to compare its output against C, so its speed claim rests on one ad-hoc measurement.
impact_assessment.benefits: Constant folding and a register fast path cut the instructions per expression; a benchmark harness makes every future speed claim checkable, and detects a C compiler only when one exists.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the optimiser must preserve wrapping arithmetic and the divide-by-zero trap, or semantics drift silently; dependency: stdlib only, C compiler optional; concurrency: none; state: benchmarks write JSON only when asked.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Fold only when semantics are identical, never fold a division whose divisor is zero, add a differential test running folded and unfolded builds, keep the C comparison opt-in and reported as unavailable when no compiler is found, and re-run every gate.

checkpoints.description: [6/6] Optimiser, benchmark harness and frame hardening complete: 92 tests pass, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed

handoff.state: optimize.py folds constants with i64 wrap and never folds a zero divisor, benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py is the only source of speed numbers, every frame slot is zeroed on entry

checkpoints.description: [1/6] Make the core values machine-checkable: a diagnostic code registry, an executable verifier, an agent capabilities manifest, a machine-code listing and a stdlib-only proof

impact_assessment.why: The stated core values (fast, no dependency, machine-level, verifiable, tested with error codes, agent-compatible) are currently claims in prose; only some are enforced by a gate.
impact_assessment.benefits: Each value becomes a command or a test an agent can run: verify proves an artifact's structure without executing it, capabilities publishes the surface as JSON, a listing shows the emitted instructions, and a test proves the compiler imports nothing outside the standard library.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new CLI subcommands and a codes registry become permanent; dependency: stdlib only must hold, so no third-party imports anywhere; concurrency: none; state: verification is read-only and never rewrites an artifact.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the registry generated from what the source emits and assert both directions against README, make verification pure over bytes, add no dependency, and run every gate.

checkpoints.description: [6/6] Implemented and verified the machine-checkable core: codes.py registry, capabilities.py manifest with three new CLI commands, verify.py with ten V codes, listing.py, stdlib-only AST proof; 113 tests pass, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed

handoff.state: capabilities/verify/listing wired into the CLI and documented
handoff.evidence: python aikit.py check cairn -> 4/4, python -m unittest discover -> 113 tests OK

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Bind the six core values (No Dependency, AI Compatible, Easily Understandable, Almost Machine Language Like, Verifiable, Error Codes) to executable evidence and a failing guard each

impact_assessment.why: The six core values are stated in prose and repeated by hand; a value with no check can silently stop being true, and an agent has no way to tell which command proves which value.
impact_assessment.benefits: One record per value with the command that demonstrates it and the test that fails when it breaks; the manifest publishes them, the README renders them, and a test asserts every guard resolves and every evidence names a real subcommand.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the value names, keys and order become permanent identifiers; dependency: stdlib only must keep holding; concurrency: none; state: read-only, values.py holds no state.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Freeze the six values and their order in an ADR, point each guard at an existing test instead of duplicating it, assert guard resolution with ast, and re-run every gate.

handoff.next: write values.py, publish in capabilities, add README table, add tests/test_values.py, then phase 4

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Six core values frozen in values.py with a proving command and a guard test each, published by capabilities and rendered in README; faster-than-C recorded as a measured goal with per-case verdicts and --strict; 124 tests pass, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed

handoff.state: values.py + tests/test_values.py, harness verdict/--strict, ADR-009 and ADR-010
